newsitem.title: USA: U.S. workers' wages, benefits up 0.6 percent.
newsitem.headline: U.S. workers' wages, benefits up 0.6 percent.

text.p: U.S. workers' compensation rose 0.6 percent in the third quarter after a 0.8 percent gain in the previous three-month period, reflecting lower growth in both pay and benefits, the Labor Department said on Tuesday.

The overall increase in compensation during the July-September period included a 0.6 percent rise in wages and salaries and a 0.6 percent rise in the cost of benefits, such as health care, received by employees, the department said.
In the second quarter, wages and salaries rose 0.9 percent and benefit costs rose 0.7 percent, the department said.
The overall increase in employee compensation costs in the third quarter, which was the smallest in a year, was below the 0.8 percent rise expected by Wall Street economists.

In the past 12 months, the department's Employment Cost Index, which measures changes in the value of wages and salaries and the cost of employee benefits for the American work force, rose by 2.8 percent, little changed from the 2.7 percent gain of the previous 12-month period.
Wages and salaries, which represent about 70 percent of the index, rose by 3.2 percent in the past 12 months, while the cost of benefits rose by 1.8 percent, it said.

The 2.8 percent increase in the ECI of the past 12 months was more moderate than the 3.5 percent gain in workers' average hourly earnings over the same period, mostly because of the slower growth of benefit costs, which are not included in average hourly earnings.

Financial markets have become hypersensitive to the prospect of tightening labour markets, which traders fear could push prices higher, and more immediately, prompt Federal Reserve policy-makers to raise interest rates to pre-empt inflationary pressures.

Compensation gains for private industry workers in the third quarter slowed to 0.6 percent from 0.8 percent in the second quarter. In the past 12 months compensation rose 2.9 percent, down from a 2.6 percent rise in the previous 12 months.

For state and local government workers, compensation rose 0.5 percent in the third quarter, down from a 0.7 percent rise in the second quarter. In the past 12 months, state and local workers' compensation rose 2.5 percent, down from a 3 percent gain in the previous 12 months.
